Charter.value: cost per conversion, lower is better
Charter.reason: The owner pays for each conversion; this is the number the business feels.

Charter.value: spend / conversions as the platform reports them; the app's count checks it on days at least 2 days old
Charter.reason: The platform counts at once; the app's count is the truth but can be up to 2 days late.

Charter.value: dollars
Charter.reason: This account spends money on clicks.
The money the owner has given so far.

Charter.value: money on tests that cannot be read
Charter.reason: The owner's limit on spending.

Charter.value: the three attributes, ad text, daily budgets, pausing
Charter.reason: What the platform lets us change (sim catalog).

Charter.value: the app, its price, the audience
Charter.reason: The owner keeps these.

Charter.value: hook: claim, question, story; visual: app-screen, hand-replay, coach-face; offer: free-trial, discount, none
Charter.reason: From sim catalog.

Charter.value: people who play poker in home games and casinos and want to make better decisions at the table
Charter.reason: From sim catalog.

Charter.value: a progress report every two weeks, written with `$readable-reports` as a Markdown file in `reports/`; the first goes out on 2026-11-16, two weeks after setup
Charter.reason: The owner asked to be left to run the climb and to hear only about money; a report every other week shows the trend without noise, and the Overview tab carries the day to day. README.md says reports go in reports/.

Charter.value: the `sim` command (see `sim catalog`)
Charter.reason: Where ads are built, launched and counted.

Charter.value: `sim attribution`, the app's own count, up to 2 days late
Charter.reason: Counts conversions independently of the platform.

Charter.value: `notify --kind money-request --json '<the request as JSON>'`
Charter.reason: README.md: to reach the owner, run notify.

Charter.value: platform conversions, checked against the app's count weekly
Charter.reason: Fast enough for tests of a few days; the weekly check catches drift between the counts.

Charter.value: hook, visual (offer held at free-trial)
Charter.reason: Hook and visual should swing results most; history's best ran a free trial, and holding it keeps nine cells the traffic can visit.

Charter.value: most money keeps earning on history's best ad; a real part keeps exploring while most of the map is untested; some develops the leans: variations of the contenders and more traffic on what looks promising
Charter.reason: Most money keeps earning from history's best; a third keeps looking while most of the map is untested; leans firm up fastest when variations and traffic build on them.

Charter.value: untested cells first, above all the coach-on-camera and story ads competitors keep running, and research-backed ideas from outside the map; more than a token test while most of the map is untested
Charter.reason: Most cells are untested and competitors change their ads monthly, so exploring must not fade.

Charter.value: directional: about 60 to 80 percent sure after discounting is enough for any move that can be undone; money moves in steps by the odds
Charter.reason: Shifting a budget or cutting an item can be reversed next tick, and waiting costs a tick of learning.

Charter.value: a lean grows strong when later reads, items and variations keep agreeing; a large move that cannot be taken back quickly waits for that
Charter.reason: First reads run hot; agreement across later results separates a pattern from luck without stopping to rerun it.

Charter.value: money follows the odds onto a new option in steps, discounted for the shrinkage leaders show once moved
Charter.reason: Leaders shrink once money moves onto them; moving in steps keeps a wrong lean cheap.

Charter.value: 30 days
Charter.reason: Competitors and the audience shift about monthly.

Charter.value: about a month: competitors in this category change their ads monthly
Charter.reason: The library's ads turn over about monthly.

Charter.value: the cheapest read that shows which way an item leans: big swings, read as soon as the counts lean, as many items at once as the money can read, compared on the same days
Charter.reason: At $15 a day an item shows which way a large gap leans within a couple of days.

Charter.value: as fast as checked items can be read, from $45 a day committed at the start of this stretch, with the best ad kept earning
Charter.reason: What limits learning here is usually how many checked items are ready, and then the money.

Charter.value: ticks every 12 hours, acting on new results each tick; step back every 24 hours; strategy and audit every 7 days; replay monthly
Charter.reason: Ticks come every 12 hours; slower reviews keep their context clean.

Charter.value: external: ticks run every 12 hours by the account's scheduler
Charter.reason: README.md says ticks are run for us.
